reason: `locator.within(other)` narrows a locator to the matches inside `other`, and Strider has no such operation. Every assertion of the test uses it

Tests the error Playwright raises when a `*` capture marker in its selector string (`*css=div >> p`) is followed by `nth`: "Can't query n-th element". Strider's locators have no capture marker, and the error exists only in Playwright's selector syntax

Tests Playwright's `*css=` capture marker inside a frame: a locator with a capture, placed in `locator(...)` after the frame prefix, keeps its capture, and a capture before a frame dive throws "Can not capture the selector before diving into the frame". Strider's locators have no capture, and a frame's locator is `page.frame(...)`

Passes a locator from another frame to `has` and expects Playwright's runtime error, "Inner "has" locator must belong to the same frame". Strider's `has` takes a RelativeLocator, which has no frame, so the mistake is a type error and doesn't compile, as EX-216 does for `toHaveURL`
Registers a custom selector engine (`playwright.selectors.register`) and counts through it while the page navigates. Strider's locators take CSS only and have no selector engines to register
The test's point is that evaluate is strict, and Locator.evaluate runs in an isolated world, which stock WebKit doesn't have
